summary:
fdev is itself a rootless Podman container using pasta networking (`/run/.containerenv` present). The `192.168.1.129` on its `enp6s0` is pasta's copy of the host address, so connecting to it from fdev reaches fdev's own namespace, which has no listener (connection refused, empty `ss`). Consequently `fsgg-store.lan` (which resolves to 192.168.1.129) loops back into fdev instead of reaching the Home receiver. The host is reachable at `169.254.1.2` (`host.containers.internal`); from fdev, 169.254.1.2:8447 was open and TLS verified against the pinned CA with `-servername fsgg-store.lan` (#4516 comment 6343424577, which corrects two earlier requests that wrongly assumed fdev shared the host network namespace). The receiver was healthy; the fault was fdev's name resolution.

Constraint: `/etc/hosts` in fdev is root-owned and read-only. A per-process override that works without changing system files or producer config: create a private mount namespace (`unshare --map-current-user --keep-caps -m`), bind-mount a private hosts file mapping `fsgg-store.lan` to 169.254.1.2 over `/etc/hosts`, then drop all capabilities (`setpriv --ambient-caps=-all --inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all`) before running the engine, so the override affects only that process (#4705; #4516 comment 6343768096). The producer endpoint and queued state stay unchanged, which matters because queued batches must not be repointed.

Limits: observations for fdev on 2026-10-22; interface addresses, the gateway alias and published ports are live and must be rechecked. This does not authorize sending or draining; each effect is admitted separately. Keep credentials out of argv and logs in any wrapper.
title: fdev is a rootless Podman container with pasta networking; fsgg-store.lan loops back unless overridden
